already-have.reason: Not already implemented and not contradicted by any recorded owner decision. (a) No ADC, TSC, COMP or analog-watchdog driver exists anywhere in the firmware: `grep -rlnE 'TSC|ADC1|ADC4|COMP1|0x4202_8000|analog watchdog|AWD' secure/src fsbl/src` returns nothing, and `hal/src/lib.rs` defines traits for Rng/Sha256/Saes/Flash/Otp/BootState/Tamp/ConsumptionMask/I2cBus/SpiBus/Buttons/Uart only — no Adc/Tsc trait. The proposal's repo evidence checks out line-for-line: `secure/src/hw/tamp.rs:199-221` sets ITAMP7E/12E/13E in CR1 with no ADC4 AWD configuration anywhere; `secure/src/hw/se_power.rs:200-232` reads back only ODR; `secure/src/board/pq1.rs:286-291` documents FLAGB PB10 as "Nothing reads it today" and `:345` lists FREE_PINS PA10/PC13/PB4; `fsbl/src/render.rs:62-72` states the verdict "never" means the user saw the fingerprint because the panel is write-only with no MISO. (b) No GitHub issue tracks it: searches for TSC, ADC, capacitance, shunt, rail current, analog watchdog, logger, probe clip, hardware trojan, interposer, implant return nothing relevant (the only "implant" hit is #5, the desoldered-OPTIGA brute-force blocker). The nearest neighbours — #248 (TAMP+CSS+PVD, uses PWR PVD not ADC4), #47/#75/#208 (TAMP HW-mode erase, escalation, BHK masking) — are the escalation sink the proposal would feed, not the sensing it proposes. (c) The only recorded position is `docs/security/user-device-verification.md:163-167`, which names "a logger on the LCD SPI bus" as an accepted residual "as for every wallet vendor" with packaging/photos/SE-CA as the layers; that is a stated residual, not an owner decision forbidding detection work, and `supply-chain-defense-research-brief.md:127` likewise lists implants as what attestation cannot prove. No memory file records a board-spin freeze, BOM freeze, or any decision against adding sense parts to EVT.
already-have.corrections: Deltas the proposal should absorb, none disqualifying: (1) Page 127 is already owned by the rdp2-self-lock first-boot journal and the OPTIGA PBS TRNG salt (CLAUDE.md invariant #3, "page 127 owns the first-boot journal and salt"), so storing the enrolled baseline there is a layout change to a quarantined candidate, not a free page — pick a page or a journal extension explicitly and make it an owner call. (2) The TSC can only measure IOs that belong to its own channel groups; I did not verify against the STM32U585CIU6 pin table (`docs/hardware/STM32U585CIU6TR Pin Functions.xls`) that SPI1 PA4/PA5/PA7, DC/RST/TE PB0/PB1/PB2, buttons PA0/PA1 and I2C PB6-PB9 are TSC-capable on this 48-pin package; several may not be, which would push part of the capacitance leg onto an ADC-based RC-discharge measurement instead and changes the board delta. (3) The pq1 bench board has no LCD panel (memory: pq1_bench_has_no_lcd), so the display-net band and the temperature/aging FPR characterisation the proposal rightly demands cannot be done on the bench unit; it needs sealed EVT units with panels, and the #705 FSBL-cannot-light-panel issue sits on the same path. (4) The AWD-to-TAMP leg should be bundled with the open TAMP work (#47 HW-mode erase, #75 escalation flip, #208 debug-triggerable-tamper masking) rather than landed alone, since tamp.rs is log-only today and an ADC4 AWD trip would currently only log. (5) The cited consumption-mask stimulus (TIM3_CH1 on PA6, NC on pq1) is confirmed unused, but the mask's own dilution is itself unmeasured (`evt-silicon-validation.md` §9), so the two measurement campaigns should share one bench setup. Novelty claim stands: no wallet vendor measures the display path; the repo has nothing, and no issue exists — this needs a new issue (surface:hardware, surface:sca-fi) if pursued.

feasible.reason: The proposal's load-bearing leg -- TSC charge-transfer on the display, button and SE nets -- cannot be realised on the pq1 package at all, and the proposal does not flag the hardware change that would be needed. On the STM32U585CIU6 (48-pin) the TSC alternate function (AF9) exists on only seven bonded pads: PB4/PB5/PB6/PB7 (group G2) and PB12/PB13/PB14 (group G1); the datasheet AF9 column is blank for PA0, PA1, PA4, PA5, PA7, PA15, PB0, PB1, PB2, PB8, PB9 and PB15. That is every net the threat names: SPI1 CS/SCK/MOSI (PA4/PA5/PA7), DC/RST/TE (PB0/PB1/PB2), LEFT/RIGHT (PA0/PA1), I2C1 to the OPTIGA (PB8/PB9) and SE_RST (PA15). The only TSC-reachable nets of interest are I2C4 SDA/SCL (PB6/PB7), and those carry external I2C pull-ups (3.3 kOhm per the EVT validation doc), which resistively load the electrode and make a charge-transfer count meaningless; measuring them 'with the SE rail OFF' additionally back-powers the SEs through their ESD diodes. So 'the only firmware-reachable mechanism that can notice a soldered tap on the write-only display bus' is false for this board: reaching the display nets would require re-pinning the display onto G1/G2 pads (and losing SE1_EN / I2C2 / RGB_EN) -- a board redesign, not a 'minimal board delta', and the proposal's 'no new silicon, TSC already on this die' framing hides it. The second leg (rail-current shunts) is also under-specified: every ADC-capable bonded pad (PA0-PA7, PB0-PB2 = ADC1_IN5..IN17) is already claimed except PA6 (consumption-mask TIM3_CH1, production-forced) and PA3 (console RX), and a mW-scale delta at 3.3 V is ~0.3 mA, which across any shunt small enough not to lift the SE/I2C ground is below one 12-bit LSB (0.8 mV) -- it needs a current-sense amplifier, and the on-die OPAMP1/2 pins (PA0/PA1/PA3, PA6/PA7/PB0) are all taken. The AWD->TAMP escalation is actively dangerous here: ITAMP7/12/13 are confirmed to be ADC4 AWD1/2/3, and a TAMP erase clears the backup registers that hold the BHK which roots the final SE050 SCP03/admin credentials; a transient on a USB-powered, supercap-backed device (plug event, dirty charger) would therefore brick the SE050 rather than perform a recoverable wipe. Placing the measurement 'before the FSBL fingerprint window' would also put a research-grade threshold into the WRP-frozen FSBL range (invariant #10), where it can never be re-tuned after RDP-2 -- the #835 halt-sink lesson made permanent. Finally, even where measurable, the defence only raises attacker cost: the panel is a module, so a swapped panel/FPC with the implant inside the COG stays inside any design band wide enough to admit lot-to-lot panel variation, and a post-enrolment implant trimmed to within the FPC's thermal drift (pF-scale) evades the self-baseline. Cost 'L' and priority 'P1' are therefore wrong: this is an XL hardware-redesign plus silicon characterisation research track with no shipped-wallet precedent, not a P1 firmware spike.
feasible.corrections: (1) Re-label kind=hardware and cost=XL: the display/button/I2C1 nets have no TSC function on the 48-pin part; sensing them means a pin re-assignment onto PB4-7/PB12-14 and a sampling capacitor pad per group (PB4 is the only free G2 pad). (2) If a firmware-only capacitance probe is wanted, the realistic substitute is GPIO RC-timing (charge the net through the internal ~25-55 kOhm pull-up, time the Schmitt crossing with TIM input capture or COMP1 on PB0/PB2 AF): it works on any pad, but the internal pull-up varies ~30% die-to-die and with temperature, so only a self-enrolled baseline is possible -- no golden-free design band, hence no detection of an implant present at enrolment -- and it cannot run with the panel unpowered (ESD clamps). (3) Rail current needs a current-sense amplifier (e.g. INA-class) plus a dedicated ADC pad; the only candidates are PA6 (would displace or share the production-forced consumption mask) or PA3 (console RX). State the real floor: tens of mA backlight-dominated LCD current makes a mW implant invisible except in a dark-screen quiet window, where a competent implant sleeps at uA. (4) Never route an AWD trip to TAMP erase on this board: it destroys BHK and with it the SE050 final credentials; at most log + refuse, and only after on-silicon FPR characterisation. (5) Keep all thresholds and the driver in the updatable secure image, never in the FSBL range; the first-boot journal/salt already owns page 127, so the baseline needs its own page or a journal extension. (6) Reframe the security claim as 'raises implant cost (visible-probe clips, naive loggers)', not 'detected unless sub-pF and battery-powered'; a module swap or trimmed series buffer defeats both the design band and the self-baseline. (7) Priority P3 / research, gated on an EVT board spin; do not couple it to IMP-01/02 as a turning of residual into detection.

vendor-claim.reason: The core precedent/novelty claim survives: no shipped wallet electrically fingerprints bus/trace capacitance or rail current, and the Trezor tree confirms it (ITAMP7/12/13 'ADC4 analog watchdog' bits are enabled in CR1 but no ADC4/TSC code exists anywhere in core/embed; the only display read-back is RDDID panel-type identification on T2T1). Ledger publishes nothing beyond SE attestation / 'secure screen driven by the SE'. The five cited sources exist and broadly support the claim, and all repo_evidence paths check out (minor line drift). However the precedent is INCOMPLETE and two load-bearing numbers/assumptions are wrong: (a) Trezor Safe 7 (T3W1) and Foundation Passport Prime DO ship hardware tamper inputs (contact/mesh, confirmed-erase), and Passport Prime's explicitly guards the display assembly, so 'Trezor/Ledger measure nothing on the display path' must be narrowed to 'nothing electrical/capacitive'; (b) the exact on-chip-touch-sensor-on-live-traces idea has a direct academic precedent not cited (Kinugawa & Hayashi, EMC Europe 2022); (c) Piliposyan's '~1 mW current floor' is the sensor RESOLUTION, not a detection floor — reliable detection is at >=40-50 mW (F1 0.88 at 5 mW), and the paper itself defers sub-5 mW/passive trojans to other techniques; (d) on the 48-pin pq1 package the TSC does not reach any of the proposal's primary nets (SPI1 LCD, DC/TE, buttons, I2C1), only PB4-PB7 and PB12-PB14 — so the proposal as written is infeasible via TSC and must fall back to GPIO-charge + ADC-decay sensing on the ADC-capable nets.
vendor-claim.corrections: PRECEDENT (narrow, do not drop): 1) Trezor Safe 7 / T3W1 ships an EXTERNAL hardware tamper input: `core/embed/models/T3W1/boards/trezor_t3w1_rev{A,B,C}.h:298/308/326 #define TAMPER_INPUT_2 1`; `core/embed/sec/tamper/stm32u5/tamper.c:157-160` sets TAMP2TRG, `:175-190 tamper_external_read()` samples PA0 (RTC_TAMP2), `:198 tamper_external_enable()` sets TAMP_CR1_TAMP2E, called only `#if PRODUCTION` from `core/embed/projects/kernel/main.c:139-142`; CR3=0 => confirmed mode (backup-domain erase). Wiring (case switch vs mesh) is not in the headers. This is contact/mesh tamper, not capacitance/current sensing — adjacent precedent only. 2) Trezor's ADC4 AWD tampers are the SAME dead letter as ours: `tamper.c:146,150-151` enable ITAMP7/12/13 with comments 'ADC4 analog watchdog monitoring 1/2/3' but `grep -rn 'ADC4|HAL_ADC_Init|ADC_HandleTypeDef' core/embed` hits only those comment lines; no TSC use anywhere (`grep -rliE 'HAL_TSC|charge.?transfer' core/embed` -> only hal_conf.h + stmpe811 touch controller). Display read-back exists only as `core/embed/io/display/st-7789/display_panel.c:70-93 display_panel_identify()` (RDDID for ILI9341 vs ST7789 panel selection, `#ifdef DISPLAY_IDENTIFY`), not integrity. Capacitance-measure strings in Trezor are ST25R3916 NFC wake-up registers (`core/embed/io/nfc/st25/.../st25r3916.c:423`), irrelevant. 3) Foundation Passport Prime (shipped 2025) advertises 'active tamper detection' that erases the Master Key; its 2025 audit response states the processor debug pads are covered by the display, 'which itself is protected by tamper detection pins that would trigger security responses upon disassembly' — i.e. a shipped wallet whose tamper system guards the display ASSEMBLY (removal), though not the display BUS electrically. SafePal S1 shipped a shield-removal sensor that Kraken Security Labs bypassed with a ground wire (blog.kraken.com, SafePal S1). Rewrite vendor_precedent to: 'No shipped wallet performs electrical (capacitance/impedance/current) self-fingerprinting of any net; Trezor Safe 7 and Passport Prime ship contact/mesh tamper pins (Passport Prime's guard the display assembly), SafePal S1 a bypassed shield switch; Ledger relies on SE attestation + SE-driven screen.' 4) Real-world implant precedent worth citing: Joe Grand, 'Reverse Engineering a Ledger Nano X Hardware Implant' (grandideastudio.com; hardwear.io USA 2026) — a field-found implant board with antenna inside a Nano X, undetected by the device. ACADEMIC PRECEDENT MISSING: Kinugawa & Hayashi, 'Board-Level Hardware Trojan Detection Using on-Chip Touch Sensor', IEEE EMC Europe 2022, DOI 10.1109/EMCEurope51680.2022.9900985 — exactly the proposal's mechanism (MCU constant-current source + ADC / touch sensor measuring capacitance AND insulation resistance of live signal traces on a populated PCB, no external equipment, before/after comparison). Cite it; it also shows the non-TSC (GPIO charge + ADC) variant that pq1 will need. The IEICE cite is correct as given: HWS2021-50, IEICE Tech. Rep. vol.121 no.206 pp.49-52, Oct 2021 (PCB individual identification from IC capacitance-sensor output variation: ADC variation + trace variation); follow-up HWS2022-4 (Kaji, Tachikake, Fujimoto, Hayashi, NAIST) reports 97.14% re-identification over 20 boards — the ken.ieice.org page is CAPTCHA-gated (HTTP 405 to fetchers), verified via search abstract only. SOURCE NUMBERS: Piliposyan & Khursheed, IEEE Trans. Computers vol.72 no.7 pp.1958-1970 (DOI 10.1109/TC.2022.3230877, accepted Dec 2022, published 2023): power sensors are 12-bit ADC with 1 mW RESOLUTION; detection F1 = 0.997 at 50 mW, >99% for P_HT >= 40 mW, 0.88 at 5 mW (LOF), with a dip at 20-40 mW; the paper states ultra-low-power/passive trojans 'should be addressed by other techniques such as visual inspection' and the earlier non-ML monitor was 'oblivious' to I/O-pin-powered trojans. Replace '~1 mW current floor' / 'mW-scale current' with 'tens-of-mW (>=40 mW reliably; 15 mW in the author's thesis), and an implant drawing from the host's I/O pins is the hard case'. PACTOR: confirmed — IEEE Spectrum 28 Feb 2024 ('last week at ISSCC' => ISSCC 2024), Columbia (Mingoo Seok lab, Mao Li, with Intel's Vivek De), 0.5 pF on processor-memory traces, first version temperature-sensitive (false alarms hot, misses cold), fixed with a temperature-selected threshold; no enrollment/FPR figures published. ImpedanceVerif: confirmed — eprint 2022/946 = TCHES 2023(1) pp.301-325 (Mosavirik, Schaumont, Tajik, WPI); it is an FPGA on-chip network analyzer over the PDN with Wasserstein-distance scoring, qualitative detection claims only, not MCU-reachable; PDNPulse (Zhu et al., IEEE TIFS 2023) is the external-instrument sibling. FEASIBILITY CORRECTION (invalidates step (1) as written): per Zephyr hal_stm32 `dts/st/u5/stm32u585ciux-pinctrl.dtsi` (ST CubeMX-derived) the 48-pin STM32U585CIUx exposes TSC only on PB4 (G2_IO1), PB5 (G2_IO2), PB6 (G2_IO3), PB7 (G2_IO4), PB12 (G1_IO1), PB13 (G1_IO2), PB14 (G1_IO3). NONE of SPI1 CS/SCK/MOSI (PA4/PA5/PA7), DC/RST/TE (PB0/PB1/PB2), LEFT/RIGHT (PA0/PA1), OPTIGA I2C1 (PB8/PB9), PA15, PB15 has a TSC function. On pq1 the TSC can therefore fingerprint only the SE050 I2C4 (PB6/PB7), SE1_EN (PB5), free PB4, and RGB_EN/I2C2 LED nets (PB12-14, `secure/src/board/pq1.rs:242,256-263`). The LCD and button nets must use the Kinugawa/Hayashi GPIO-charge + ADC-decay method: ADC inputs exist on PA0 (ADC1_IN5), PA1 (ADC1_IN6), PA4 (ADC1/4_IN9), PA5 (ADC1/4_IN10), PA6 (ADC1/4_IN11, NC on pq1 — usable only if the board routes a shunt-sense there), PA7 (ADC1_IN12/ADC4_IN20), PB0 (ADC1_IN15/ADC4_IN18), PB1 (ADC1_IN16/ADC4_IN19), PB2 (ADC1_IN17). PB8/PB9 (OPTIGA I2C1) have neither TSC nor ADC — the OPTIGA bus cannot be self-fingerprinted on this package without a board change. Also every TSC group needs one sampling-capacitor pin from the same group (G2 would consume one of PB4-7), and TSC pins must be configured open-drain with Schmitt trigger disabled, which conflicts with I2C4's live function (measure only with the SE rail off, as proposed). REPO EVIDENCE: all verified; line drift: `secure/src/board/pq1.rs:292-294` (FLAGB PB10 'Nothing reads it today'), not 286-291; `secure/src/hw/tamp.rs:287-299` sets ITAMP7/12/13 in CR1 and `:304-321` mirrors them in IER (constants at 199-204); `grep -rlnE 'TSC|ADC1|ADC4|COMP1|0x4202_8000' secure/src fsbl/src` -> no matches confirmed; `secure/src/hw/se_power.rs:196-232` read-back is ODR confirmed; `fsbl/src/render.rs:62-72` 'cannot observe the panel' confirmed. No repo doc already covers capacitance/current self-fingerprinting (grep over docs/ hits only pull-up/decoupling capacitance), so IMP-03 is genuinely new to the repo.
